parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim from the second subcase (all pieces of Q at most τ) of Theorem B's inductive step. There the text needs D(M)≥1 and derives it from the asserted dichotomy D(Q)≤D(P)-1 or D(Q)≥D(P)+1, justified only by 'reverse-parity ... even with respect to the unit lattice generated by the lowest dyadic'. But cuts may be placed at arbitrary real points, so the piece lengths, and hence D(P), D(Q), are arbitrary reals; no integrality or dyadic lattice constrains them, and nothing in the text proves any such quantization. The reverse triangle inequality (Lemma A) only gives D(M)≥|D(P)-D(Q)|, which can be near 0 (e.g. D(Q) close to D(P)), so it cannot yield D(M)≥1. Elsewhere only n≤3 numerical checks are offered, so obligation (L) is not established for all n.
